desc:
A company has k identical meeting rooms. Each request is a half-open range [start, end), so a room can host a meeting that starts exactly when the previous one in that room ends. A room hosts one meeting at a time, and a meeting must be held entirely in a single room.

You may reject requests. Return the largest number of requests that can be held.

meetings = [[1, 4], [2, 5], [3, 6], [4, 7]], k = 2  ->  3

For example hold [1, 4] and [4, 7] in one room and [2, 5] in the other.
constraints: The requests are in no particular order
hints: With k = 1 this is activity selection: sort by end time and take every meeting that fits. How can this be extended to several rooms?
Process meetings by increasing end time. A meeting that can be placed should be placed; the question is which room to put it in.

Put it into the room that became free latest but still not after the meeting's start (best fit). That keeps the rooms that are free earlier available for meetings with earlier starts. Keep the free-from times of the k rooms in a sorted list and binary search it.
editorial: Generalised activity selection. Sort meetings by end time (ties by start). Maintain, for each of the k rooms, the time since which it is free (initially 0). For the next meeting [s, e) look for the room with the largest free-time that is still at most s. If one exists, hold the meeting there and set that room's free-time to e; if none exists, every room is busy at s and the meeting is rejected.

Why best fit: among rooms that can take the meeting, using the one that was free the latest wastes the least idle time, and the other rooms (free earlier) stay compatible with a superset of the remaining meetings. An exchange argument shows that this never loses a meeting compared with an optimal schedule, because all later meetings end no earlier than the current one.

Keep the free-times in a sorted list: bisect_right(free, s) gives the number of rooms free by time s; remove the last of them, insert e with insort. With k ≤ 100 each list operation is cheap. Total time O(n log n + n k) at worst, space O(k) beyond the sorted copy. As a sanity check, an accepted set is feasible exactly when no moment is covered by more than k accepted meetings.
solution:
from bisect import bisect_right, insort


def maxMeetingsKRooms(meetings, k):
    free = [0] * k
    count = 0
    for s, e in sorted(meetings, key=lambda m: (m[1], m[0])):
        i = bisect_right(free, s)
        if i:
            free.pop(i - 1)
            insort(free, e)
            count += 1
    return count
